requirement.evidence: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:
requirement.note: Document bans landlords from paying for coordinator services, bans parallel pricing coordination, and requires the AG to set up a complaint location. The card's wording is a plainer paraphrase and is adequate.

key_value.evidence: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
key_value.note: Ban on using or providing coordination services, and violation of the NJ Antitrust Act, are both stated (4.b and 4.e cover providers).

effective_date.evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
effective_date.note: Document is approved July 20, 2026 and the effective date is computed. The twelfth month following July 2026 is July 2027, so 2027-07-01 follows by a small step. The document does not state the calendar date directly.

status.evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
status.note: As of 2026-10-01, the computed effective date of 2027-07-01 is in the future, so not_yet_effective fits.

coverage.note: Coverage is empty on the card.

citation.note: P.L. 2026, c.43 and A3497 ACS 1R are supported. The header also shows C.56:9-20 to 56:9-26 for §§1-7, so the N.J.S.A. range matches. It is partly supported because the document names the chapter as Assembly Committee Substitute First Reprint for A3497, and the reprint wording is paraphrased.
